input.question: If black boxes have such critical information why can't we relay it to land in real time?
input.ground_truth: As important as that information is, the cost of streaming it constantly from a plane is probably an uneccessary one for most airlines. It takes a lot of data to stream voice data and instrument data constantly over a flight and depending on the route taken, their best coverage might be a satellite link which is too slow for the task. Crashes just don't happen nearly enough for that much redundancy to be paid for since it does nothing to improve the immediate safety of flight, and adding complexity to something that works relatively well might not always be a great idea. So the bottom line is probably airlines are too cheap to afford such a luxury feature. Though I believe some flights have started using that technology it is far from becoming commonplace

Okay! Imagine the black box in a plane is like a little notebook that writes down everything that happens on the plane.

Now, the reason we can't send all the notebook's writing to the ground right away is because the plane is flying super high and really fast. Sending all that writing (which is a lot of information!) needs a big, strong connection, like a really long straw that can send tiny messages. But sometimes, the straw isn't strong enough or long enough, or there isn't a good place on the ground to catch all the messages.

So, instead of sending everything right away, the black box just keeps writing in its notebook, and when the plane lands (or if something bad happens), we can get the notebook and see what was written. That way, we don't lose any of the important information.

But scientists and engineers are working on making those "straws" better, so maybe one day we can send all the information in real time!
